editor_note: The translation is faithful and natural, uses the informal "kamu" and "AI-mu" consistently, and keeps "skill AI" throughout, a reasonable choice. Entry [5], "memberi tahu di mana skill tersebut harus diterapkan", keeps the meaning of the English.

Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally: [24] "Kami memperkirakan ukuran blok yang didukung akan bertambah secara bertahap" keeps the English's forward-looking hedge, and [38] "Sitasi ... fitur berbasis AI apa pun ... penelitianmu" keeps the informal kamu register and matches the page's "berbasis AI" wording.

None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 7 puts "optionally" as "(opsional)" at the end of the sentence and keeps the meaning. Entry 14 correctly says the same value becomes the "batas penggunaan" and that you can set it higher with `usage_allocation_seconds`. The only defect is in entry 16: in each of the three list items, the sentence-final period has moved inside the link text ("[instans.]", "[meminimalkan penggunaan job.]", "[scheduler fair-share.]"). That makes the period part of each link, which a native editor would move back outside the brackets.

examples.source: - Learn about [instances](/guides/instances).
examples.translation: - Pelajari tentang [instans.](/guides/instances)
examples.suggested: - Pelajari tentang [instans](/guides/instances).
examples.why: The sentence-final period was moved inside the link text in all three list items, so each period becomes part of the link. Move it back outside, as in the source.

editor_note: Entry 5, the rewritten permission table, is faithful row for row. Every permission maps to the right action, and the Get/List/Cancel/Run/Delete verbs come through as Mendapatkan/Menampilkan daftar/Membatalkan/Menjalankan/Menghapus. The one slip is "Close job session", which became "Menutup job Session". Indonesian puts the head noun first, so "job Session" reads as "the session's job" when it should mean "the job session". It should be "Menutup Session job". The endpoint path (DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}/close) makes the real meaning clear, so it will not mislead anyone, but a native editor would fix the word order.

examples.source: Close job session (`DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}/close`)
examples.translation: Menutup job Session (`DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}/close`)
examples.suggested: Menutup Session job (`DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}/close`)
examples.why: English word order was carried over unchanged. In Indonesian the head noun comes first, so 'job Session' means a job belonging to a Session. The action closes the session, not a job.

editor_note: None of the 7 rewritten entries changes the meaning. Entry 47 keeps the caveat that NoiseModel does not support non-local errors and keeps the advice to write a TransformationPass. The problem is inconsistent terms. The rewrites in [37], [47] and [48] use the English word order "noise model" and "quantum error". Entry [9] and the first half of the page (entries 0–35) use Indonesian order: "model noise" and "error kuantum". So the same two concepts appear in two forms across the page. Entry [47] also has the stiff phrase "quantum error non-lokal untuk qubit" ("non-local quantum error for qubits"). The English means errors on non-local qubits, so the modifier is misplaced.

examples.source: When adding a quantum error to a noise model, we must specify the type of *instruction*...
examples.translation: Saat menambahkan quantum error ke noise model, kita harus menentukan jenis *instruksi*...
examples.suggested: Saat menambahkan error kuantum ke model noise, kita harus menentukan jenis *instruksi*...
examples.why: Entries 0–35 and entry [9] consistently use 'model noise' / 'error kuantum'. This rewrite switches to English word order, so the page uses both forms for the same terms.

examples.source: `NoiseModel` does not support addition of non-local qubit quantum errors.
examples.translation: `NoiseModel` tidak mendukung penambahan quantum error non-lokal untuk qubit.
examples.suggested: `NoiseModel` tidak mendukung penambahan error kuantum pada qubit non-lokal.
examples.why: 'non-lokal untuk qubit' is a stiff calque and puts the modifier in the wrong place. The English means errors that act on non-local qubits, and it keeps the English 'quantum error' order, unlike the first half of the page.

examples.source: Execute a noisy simulation with a noise model
examples.translation: Menjalankan simulasi bernoise dengan noise model
examples.suggested: Menjalankan simulasi bernoise dengan model noise
examples.why: The heading uses 'noise model', but entries [0], [1], [9] and [17] use 'model noise'. The term should be the same across the whole page.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries match the English: entry 8 renders the install caveat as "instal [pustaka `graphviz`] untuk fungsi plotting DAG", and entry 10 keeps the conditional $R_Z$ rotation as "tergantung pada hasil pengukuran", consistent with "sirkuit" elsewhere on the page.

Both rewritten entries keep the meaning of the English. Entry 7 still covers idle qubits, noise cancellation, decoherence suppression and the NMR refocusing analogy, and entry 13 still says the gates compose to the identity, are spaced regularly and that XY4 has four gates. In entry 7, though, "sequence" is translated two ways in one sentence: "pulse sequences" becomes "rangkaian pulsa" and "dynamical decoupling sequences" becomes "urutan dynamical decoupling". Entry 13 then uses "urutan", and "rangkaian" is also the usual Indonesian word for a circuit. Entry 7 also changes the cited paper's title in the link text to "Superconducting qubits", when it should stay "Superconducting Qubits".

examples.source: adding pulse sequences (known as _dynamical decoupling sequences_) ... These pulse sequences are similar to refocusing pulses
examples.translation: menambahkan rangkaian pulsa (dikenal sebagai _urutan dynamical decoupling_) ... Rangkaian pulsa ini mirip dengan refocusing pulse
examples.suggested: menambahkan urutan pulsa (dikenal sebagai _urutan dynamical decoupling_) ... Urutan pulsa ini mirip dengan refocusing pulse
examples.why: One sentence translates 'sequence' two ways. 'Rangkaian' is also the usual Indonesian word for 'circuit', so using 'urutan' throughout, as entry 13 does, is clearer.

examples.source: [A Quantum Engineer's Guide to Superconducting Qubits](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06560)
examples.translation: [A Quantum Engineer's Guide to Superconducting qubits](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06560)
examples.suggested: [A Quantum Engineer's Guide to Superconducting Qubits](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06560)
examples.why: This is the title of a cited English paper and should be copied exactly. The capital Q in 'Qubits' was changed to lowercase.

editor_note: Entry 6 keeps the English meaning: "beban kerja yang divektorisasi", PUB kept as a term, "dijalankan sebagai sebuah job", and results that depend on both "PUB yang digunakan serta opsi runtime". The informal "kamu" register holds.

All 23 rewritten entries match the English. The precedence logic in [25], [26], [35] and [36] is intact: "Nilai ini diutamakan di atas nilai apa pun yang ditentukan sebagai opsi", and the job fails when num_randomizations × shots_per_randomization "lebih kecil dari" the shots needed. The "Dokumentasi API `…`" links and the terms primitif, shot and job are used consistently.

None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 6 ("Konstruk paling dasar yang menerima alokasi waktu dari akun induk…") and entry 11 ("instance dengan jumlah menit dua kali lipat dapat mengeksekusi workload dua kali lebih banyak") say the same thing as the English. Entry 14 adds a gloss that is not in the source: "workload tertua (yang paling lama menunggu)". It is accurate under FIFO, but it is still an addition. The same entry also ends a little abruptly with "berdasarkan first-in-first-out (FIFO)", where a native editor would write "berdasarkan prinsip first-in-first-out (FIFO)".

examples.source: the scheduler will select the oldest workload first
examples.translation: penjadwal akan memilih workload tertua (yang paling lama menunggu) terlebih dahulu
examples.suggested: penjadwal akan memilih workload tertua terlebih dahulu
examples.why: The added parenthetical is not in the source. It is accurate, so it does not mislead, but it is an editorial addition that should be dropped.

examples.source: the scheduler works on a first-in-first-out (FIFO) basis
examples.translation: penjadwal bekerja berdasarkan first-in-first-out (FIFO)
examples.suggested: penjadwal bekerja berdasarkan prinsip first-in-first-out (FIFO)
examples.why: 'berdasarkan' followed directly by an English term reads clipped. Adding 'prinsip' (or 'asas') renders 'basis' naturally.

editor_note: None of the 9 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The numbers, conditions and caveats are all intact, including 100 randomizations x 200 shots = 20.000 shot, 26,8 juta instruksi applied "per job bukan per PUB", and the dictionary that "mengganti default secara keseluruhan". Entry 49 uses two words for entanglement in one sentence: "entanglement rendah" and then "keterjeratannya lebih tinggi". In the entry 39 table, "owns" is translated literally as possession: "`reps` dan `time` dimiliki oleh fungsi ini" and "ditolak, karena jalur eksekusi memilikinya". Those lines don't clearly tell the reader that the function sets these values itself. Entry 31 has two stiff phrasings: "Hal lainnya harus datang secara transitif" and "adalah yang menginstal".

examples.source: Early, low-entanglement steps compress well ...; later, more-entangled steps need a deeper one.
examples.translation: Langkah-langkah awal dengan entanglement rendah ...; langkah-langkah selanjutnya yang keterjeratannya lebih tinggi ...
examples.suggested: ... langkah-langkah selanjutnya dengan entanglement lebih tinggi membutuhkan ansatz yang lebih dalam.
examples.why: One concept is named two ways (entanglement / keterjeratan) in a single sentence. Use one term consistently.

examples.source: `reps` and `time` are owned by the function. ... `backend` and `target` are rejected, since the execution path owns them.
examples.translation: `reps` dan `time` dimiliki oleh fungsi ini. ... `backend` dan `target` ditolak, karena jalur eksekusi memilikinya.
examples.suggested: `reps` dan `time` ditentukan oleh fungsi ini. ... `backend` dan `target` ditolak, karena keduanya ditentukan oleh jalur eksekusi.
examples.why: Translating 'owns' as possession (dimiliki/memilikinya) is a calque. It hides the point that the user cannot set these values.

examples.source: Anything else must arrive transitively ... `qiskit-addon-aqc-tensor[quimb-jax]` is what installs `quimb` and `jax`.
examples.translation: Hal lainnya harus datang secara transitif ... `qiskit-addon-aqc-tensor[quimb-jax]` adalah yang menginstal `quimb` dan `jax`.
examples.suggested: Paket lain harus terpasang secara transitif ... `qiskit-addon-aqc-tensor[quimb-jax]`-lah yang menginstal `quimb` dan `jax`.
examples.why: 'Hal lainnya harus datang' and 'adalah yang menginstal' are literal renderings of the English structure. A native technical writer would say 'Paket lain' and use '-lah' for emphasis.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries (4, 5, 6, 20, 27) would mislead a learner. Entry 4 keeps all five techniques and the resilience_level cost/accuracy trade-off, and entry 6 keeps both "sebagian besar" (largely) and the note that the import statement is the only change. Two small wording issues remain. In entry 5, "finer control" became "kontrol yang lebih baik" ("better control"), which drops the idea of more fine-grained control. In entry 6, "dengan satu-satunya perubahan adalah pernyataan import" copies the English sentence structure and reads stiffly.

examples.source: Running on the client side provides greater transparency, faster debugging feedback, and finer control.
examples.translation: ... umpan balik debugging yang lebih cepat, dan kontrol yang lebih baik.
examples.suggested: ... umpan balik debugging yang lebih cepat, dan kontrol yang lebih terperinci.
examples.why: 'finer' means more fine-grained, not 'better'. The translation loses that nuance, though a learner would not come away with a false idea.

examples.source: with the only change being the import statement.
examples.translation: dengan satu-satunya perubahan adalah pernyataan import.
examples.suggested: karena yang perlu diubah hanyalah pernyataan import.
examples.why: This copies the English 'with X being Y' structure word for word, which is not natural Indonesian. A native technical writer would restructure the clause.

editor_note: Entry 11, the rewritten method table, keeps the meaning of all four rows, including the note that job.result() blocks until the job finishes. It does not mislead. One phrasing problem: "Memblokir hingga job mencapai keadaan terminal" copies "terminal state" word for word. That clashes with the page's own "status job" wording. It also breaks the imperative verbs used in the other rows (Periksa/Dapatkan/Ambil). A native editor would write something like "Blokir hingga job mencapai status akhir".

examples.source: Block until the job reaches a terminal state
examples.translation: Memblokir hingga job mencapai keadaan terminal
examples.suggested: Blokir hingga job mencapai status akhir (final)
examples.why: "keadaan terminal" copies "terminal state" word for word. The rest of the page calls job states "status" (Pending/Completed/Failed), so "status akhir" is clearer and matches. "Memblokir" also breaks the imperative pattern of the other rows.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (5, 16, 24, 28) would mislead a learner. Note 7 (entry 24) keeps every point: transpiling is required, custom `gate` definitions and gate modifiers cannot run as-is, gate modifiers are evaluated eagerly during parsing, and there may be a runtime cost. Two things are still worth a fix. In entry 24, "proses `transpile` akan menyelesaikannya menjadi circuit ISA" copies English "resolves them into" word for word, and "menyelesaikan" reads as "finish/solve"; "mengubahnya menjadi" is more natural. In entry 28, the rewrite adds a 4-space indent to every list item inside the Admonition, which the English does not have and which may render as a code block instead of a list. Entries 5 and 16 are faithful, and entry 16 only translates the table header row ("Fitur OpenQASM 3", "Catatan").

examples.source: but the `transpile` process resolves them into valid ISA circuits
examples.translation: tetapi proses `transpile` akan menyelesaikannya menjadi circuit ISA yang valid
examples.suggested: tetapi proses `transpile` akan mengubahnya menjadi circuit ISA yang valid
examples.why: 'menyelesaikan ... menjadi' is a word-for-word copy of 'resolve into' and reads as 'finish/solve'. 'Mengubah(nya) menjadi' is what an Indonesian technical writer would use for this conversion.

examples.source: - Learn how to generate OpenQASM code using [IBM Quantum Composer](/guides/composer).
examples.translation: - Pelajari cara menghasilkan kode OpenQASM menggunakan [IBM Quantum Composer](/guides/composer).
examples.suggested: - Pelajari cara menghasilkan kode OpenQASM menggunakan [IBM Quantum Composer](/guides/composer).
examples.why: The rewrite adds a 4-space indent to each list item that the English does not have. This may render as a code block instead of a list, so the items should start at column zero like the source.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries (11, 14, 20, 23, 40) would mislead a learner. The removal of c_if, the removal of Instruction.duration/unit and the advice to move to estimate_duration all keep their conditions and caveats. There are two small slips. In entry 14, "strictly less featureful" becomes "jelas lebih terbatas fiturnya", which loses the technical sense that c_if is a strict subset of full control flow. In entry 20, "memperlambat bahkan operasi Circuit" copies the English word order, where natural Indonesian puts "bahkan" before the verb.

examples.line_approx: Cara ini jelas lebih terbatas fiturnya
examples.source: This was strictly less featureful than the full control-flow form
examples.translation: Cara ini jelas lebih terbatas fiturnya dibandingkan bentuk control-flow penuh
examples.suggested: Fitur cara ini sepenuhnya merupakan subset dari (selalu lebih sedikit daripada) bentuk control-flow penuh
examples.why: 'strictly' here means c_if could do nothing that if_test could not do (a strict subset). 'jelas' only means 'clearly', so it keeps the claim but loses that point.

examples.source: slowed down even circuit operations that did not directly need to touch the information
examples.translation: memperlambat bahkan operasi Circuit yang tidak secara langsung perlu menyentuh informasi tersebut
examples.suggested: bahkan memperlambat operasi Circuit yang sebenarnya tidak perlu mengakses informasi tersebut secara langsung
examples.why: The placement of 'bahkan' copies the English order and reads stiffly. The verb 'menyentuh' is also a literal calque of 'touch'.

editor_note: Entry 25 keeps the English meaning, including both "always" claims ("transpiler selalu bisa membalik arah Gate", "selalu bisa direpresentasikan ... meskipun konektivitasnya terbatas, dengan menyisipkan Gate SWAP"), and renders "directional" as "bersifat terarah", which matches entry 44.

The three rewritten entries (9, 15, 17) keep the meaning of the English. Every IBM-versus-user split, the "IBM tidak bertanggung jawab atas pencadangan…" disclaimers and the "jika tersedia" and "sesuai kebutuhan" caveats are all intact. Two stiff spots are left. In entry 9, "Menyediakan ketersediaan" repeats the root "sedia" and reads as a literal calque of "provide availability". In entry 15, "layanan yang aman yang mematuhi" stacks two "yang" clauses in a way a native editor would smooth out.

examples.source: Provide availability and tools for major version updates.
examples.translation: Menyediakan ketersediaan dan alat untuk pembaruan versi mayor.
examples.suggested: Menyediakan versi mayor baru beserta alat untuk melakukan pembaruannya.
examples.why: 'Menyediakan ketersediaan' uses the root 'sedia' twice and is a word-for-word calque of 'provide availability'. It reads robotically in Indonesian.

examples.source: Provide a secure service that complies with key standards.
examples.translation: Menyediakan layanan yang aman yang mematuhi standar-standar utama.
examples.suggested: Menyediakan layanan aman yang mematuhi standar-standar utama.
examples.why: The double 'yang' is stiff translationese. Dropping the first 'yang' reads more naturally and keeps the meaning.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally. "error mitigation and error suppression" is rendered consistently as "mitigasi error dan penekanan error", the overhead caveat in [6] is kept intact ("overhead pra-pemrosesan ... keseimbangan"), and the informal "hasilmu/jobmu" register holds.

Both rewritten entries are faithful and natural: entry 5 renders "tracked against the parent Qiskit Serverless job" as "dicatat pada job Qiskit Serverless induk" and keeps the get_runtime_service()/QiskitRuntimeService() contrast intact, and entry 27's "memaparkan bagaimana para peneliti memanfaatkan" conveys the paper reference accurately.

All three rewritten entries (7, 12, 13) keep the meaning of the English, and none would mislead a learner. Entry 13 is faithful, including the 100-qubit verification example and its caveats. There are three small wording problems. In entry 7, "restricted class" became "kelas khusus" ("special class") where "kelas terbatas" would be accurate, and "Clifford Circuit" keeps English word order instead of the Indonesian head-first "Circuit Clifford". In entry 12, "up to global phase" became "hingga suatu fase global", a calque that can read as "until a global phase". "dengan mengabaikan fase global" or "sampai dengan fase global" would be clearer.

examples.source: an important restricted class of quantum circuits
examples.translation: merupakan kelas khusus Circuit kuantum yang penting
examples.suggested: merupakan kelas terbatas Circuit kuantum yang penting
examples.why: 'khusus' means special or particular, not restricted. It loses the idea that this is a limited subclass of circuits, which is the reason it can be simulated efficiently. The shift is small and does not mislead.

examples.source: also known as Clifford circuits
examples.translation: yang juga dikenal sebagai Clifford Circuit
examples.suggested: yang juga dikenal sebagai Circuit Clifford
examples.why: This keeps English modifier-before-noun order. Indonesian puts the head noun first, and the same sentence already writes 'Circuit stabilizer'.

examples.source: (up to global phase)
examples.translation: (hingga suatu fase global)
examples.suggested: (dengan mengabaikan fase global)
examples.why: This calques the math idiom 'up to'. 'hingga' literally means 'until', so the phrase reads awkwardly and hides that the phase is being ignored.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are accurate and natural: entry 5 keeps the survey request in the informal kamu register ("Masukanmu akan kami gunakan…"), and entry 12 keeps every clause of the Credly notice, including the data list "nama, alamat email, dan lencana yang diperoleh" and the caveat "IBM mungkin membagikan… secara global".

Entry 29 matches the Credly notice clause by clause, including "pemroses data pihak ketiga yang diotorisasi oleh IBM", the list "(nama, alamat email, dan lencana yang diperoleh)", the hedged "IBM mungkin membagikan" and "anak perusahaan IBM dan pihak ketiga secara global", and it keeps the informal "kamu/-mu" register.

None of the 7 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The threshold condition (p < 1/C), the Cp^2 bound, the 3,23% Shor figure and the 0,1%–1% surface-code estimate all match the English. A native editor would still fix a few calques and word choices. "some constant power" / "some fixed positive real number" become "beberapa" ("several") in entries 4 and 11 where "suatu" is meant. "of arbitrary size" is rendered "ukuran sembarangan", which suggests carelessness; "ukuran sembarang" is the correct word. Entry 6 says "kepentingan praktis" where "arti penting praktis" is meant, and entry 12 turns "a natural thing to do" into the obligation-sounding "Hal alami yang harus dilakukan".

examples.source: some constant power of the logarithm of $N$
examples.translation: beberapa pangkat konstan dari logaritma $N$
examples.suggested: suatu pangkat konstan dari logaritma $N$
examples.why: 'beberapa' means 'several'; the English 'some' here means one unspecified constant, which is 'suatu'. The same calque appears in entry 11 ('beberapa bilangan real positif tetap $C$').

examples.source: reliable quantum circuits of arbitrary size ... great practical importance
examples.translation: Circuit kuantum yang andal dengan ukuran sembarangan ... kepentingan praktis yang besar
examples.suggested: sirkuit kuantum yang andal dengan ukuran sembarang ... arti penting praktis yang besar
examples.why: 'sembarangan' means careless or haphazard, while 'sembarang' is the mathematical 'arbitrary'. 'kepentingan' means interest or stake, not significance.

examples.source: A natural thing to do at this point is to choose a better code
examples.translation: Hal alami yang harus dilakukan pada titik ini adalah memilih kode yang lebih baik
examples.suggested: Langkah yang wajar pada titik ini adalah memilih kode yang lebih baik
examples.why: 'Hal alami yang harus dilakukan' is a literal calque, and 'harus' makes it sound like an obligation. 'Langkah yang wajar' is the idiomatic phrasing.

examples.source: those details will not be communicated here
examples.translation: detail tersebut tidak akan dikomunikasikan di sini
examples.suggested: detail tersebut tidak akan dibahas di sini
examples.why: 'dikomunikasikan' is a stiff calque. An Indonesian technical writer would say 'dibahas'.

editor_note: Entry 47 is faithful: "tidak setiap lingkaran tertutup kesalahan $X$ terkandung dalam stabilizer" keeps the negation's scope, and the 'garis kisi horizontal/vertikal' definition (a full row/column, not the loop's segments) is intact and uses the same terms as the rest of the file (lingkaran tertutup, kisi periodik).

I found no meaning drift in the 15 rewritten entries. The key logic survives, including the "at least one -1" syndrome rule (110), the commute-but-undetected second case (118/123) and the O(n^2/log n) Clifford encoder bound (105). The main problem is terminology that varies between entries. The prose entries 110, 118 and 123 are a single sequence, yet 110 uses "sindrom", "generator stabilizer" and "observabel", while 118 and 123 switch to "syndrome", "stabilizer generator", "code space" and "3-bit repetition code". 161 also uses "stabilizer codes" although 102/104 have "kode stabilizer" and "ruang kode". Smaller points: "fixed by" is rendered as "tetap tak berubah oleh" in 10 but as "ditetapkan oleh" in 22, which reads as "determined by". 100 leaves "standard basis states/measurements" in English even though the page elsewhere uses "basis standar". 105 has the word order "membutuhkan gate $O(n^2/\log(n))$". 161 adds italic emphasis on "*baik*" that is not in the source, and "dalam aksi" is a calque.

examples.source: because $E$ commutes with every stabilizer generator, the syndrome is $(+1,\ldots,+1)$
examples.translation: karena $E$ komutatif dengan setiap stabilizer generator, syndrome-nya adalah $(+1,\ldots,+1)$
examples.suggested: karena $E$ komutatif dengan setiap generator stabilizer, sindromnya adalah $(+1,\ldots,+1)$
examples.why: Entry 110, just before it, uses 'generator stabilizer' and 'sindrom', and 102/104 use 'ruang kode' for code space. These rewritten entries switch back and forth within the same section.

examples.source: at least one nonzero vector is fixed by all of the stabilizer generators
examples.translation: setidaknya ada satu vektor tak-nol yang ditetapkan oleh semua generator stabilizer
examples.suggested: setidaknya ada satu vektor tak-nol yang tidak berubah oleh semua generator stabilizer
examples.why: 'Ditetapkan oleh' reads as 'determined/set by' rather than 'left invariant by'. Entry 10 already uses the better 'tetap tak berubah oleh'.

examples.source: Performing Clifford operations on standard basis states followed by standard basis measurements
examples.translation: Melakukan operasi Clifford pada standard basis states diikuti dengan standard basis measurements
examples.suggested: Melakukan operasi Clifford pada state basis standar, diikuti pengukuran dalam basis standar,
examples.why: These English phrases were left untranslated in running prose, although the page elsewhere uses 'basis standar'.

examples.source: using a Clifford operation that requires $O(n^2/\log(n))$ gates
examples.translation: menggunakan operasi Clifford yang membutuhkan gate $O(n^2/\log(n))$
examples.suggested: menggunakan operasi Clifford yang membutuhkan $O(n^2/\log(n))$ gate
examples.why: With the quantity after the noun, the phrase reads as the name of a gate rather than a gate count.

examples.source: We'll see this artistry on display in the next lesson.
examples.translation: Kita akan melihat seni ini dalam aksi di pelajaran berikutnya.
examples.suggested: Kita akan melihat seni ini diterapkan di pelajaran berikutnya.
examples.why: 'Dalam aksi' is a calque. The added italics on '*baik*' in the same entry are also not in the source.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 9 is faithful: matriks densitas, channel and pengukuran are kept consistent, and "keduanya" correctly points back to jarak/kemiripan. Entry 12 has a passive calque, "kamu akan diberitahu oleh Credly", and "diberitahu" should be written "diberi tahu" in standard spelling. It also adds "seluruh" (all lessons), a small strengthening the English does not have. Entry 6, "Dasar-dasar algoritma kuantum", uses the same "Dasar-dasar" as "Basics" in entry 5, but the two titles are still easy to tell apart, so that choice is acceptable.

examples.source: you will be notified by Credly that you have earned a badge.
examples.translation: kamu akan diberitahu oleh Credly bahwa kamu telah mendapatkan lencana.
examples.suggested: Credly akan memberi tahu kamu bahwa kamu telah mendapatkan lencana.
examples.why: This copies the English passive with 'oleh'. An active sentence reads more naturally in Indonesian, and standard spelling is 'diberi tahu', not 'diberitahu'.

examples.source: This exam is intended to be taken after reading the lessons in this course.
examples.translation: Ujian ini sebaiknya diikuti setelah kamu membaca seluruh pelajaran dalam kursus ini.
examples.suggested: Ujian ini sebaiknya diikuti setelah kamu membaca pelajaran-pelajaran dalam kursus ini.
examples.why: 'seluruh' (all) is not in the English. It slightly strengthens the recommendation, but it does not mislead.

editor_note: Entries 4 and 5 are faithful and read naturally. Entry 4 keeps *channel* as the term and uses *saluran komunikasi* for the information-theory sense, which is the same distinction the English draws. Entry 3 has two small problems. First, "diskrit-waktu" keeps the English word order; the usual Indonesian term is "waktu diskrit", as in "sistem waktu diskrit". Second, the tooltip turns "infinitesimally small time periods" into "periode waktu yang sangat kecil" ("very small time periods"), which weakens the calculus meaning. The tooltip also says "berbeda" twice in a row ("yang berbeda, berbeda dengan"). None of this would mislead a learner.

examples.source: discrete-time change
examples.translation: perubahan ... yang diskrit-waktu
examples.suggested: perubahan keadaan waktu diskrit apa pun yang bisa direalisasikan secara fisik
examples.why: 'diskrit-waktu' keeps the English modifier order. The usual Indonesian technical term is 'waktu diskrit'.

examples.source: as opposed to a continuous process that can be described over infinitesimally small time periods
examples.translation: berbeda dengan proses kontinu yang bisa dideskripsikan selama periode waktu yang sangat kecil
examples.suggested: lain halnya dengan proses kontinu yang dapat dideskripsikan pada selang waktu yang infinitesimal (sangat kecil tak hingga)
examples.why: 'sangat kecil' ('very small') loses the calculus meaning of 'infinitesimal'. It also repeats 'berbeda' right after 'yang berbeda'. This is a small softening and does not mislead.

editor_note: Entry 70 matches the English: "padanan klasiknya (yang hanya bisa berada dalam state 0 atau 1)" keeps the contrast with classical bits, and "jumlah operasi berurutan ... termasuk sebagian interaksi dengan sumber daya komputasi klasikal, misalnya saat memuat parameter dari rangkaian" keeps the CLOPS caveat, with "rangkaian" used for circuit as in the rest of the page.

The five rewritten entries (5, 7, 8, 9, 12) match the English and use the informal "kamu" register consistently; the pass rule "minimal 16 dengan benar", the lockout "dalam dua percobaan, ujian akan terkunci sementara" and the Credly notice ("anak perusahaan dan pihak ketiga IBM di seluruh dunia") are all accurate.

Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. In [7], "badging exam" becomes "ujian untuk mendapatkan badge", and in [11] the privacy notice keeps every element: "pemroses data pihak ketiga yang diberi wewenang oleh IBM", the list of data shared with Credly, the hedge "IBM dapat membagikan" for "may share", and "anak perusahaan IBM".

Entry 12 is faithful and uses the informal "kamu" register. Every point in the privacy notice survives, including "prosesor data pihak ketiga yang telah diotorisasi oleh IBM", the shared data list "(nama, alamat email, dan badge yang diperoleh)" and "dapat berbagi ... di seluruh dunia".

None of the 18 rewritten entries misleads a learner. The dt-underestimation caveat (151), the Rayleigh-Ritz upper-bound argument (258) and the conditions where KQD applies (223/226) all keep their meaning. Three wording slips remain. In 232, "Temporarily assume" became "Sementara itu anggap", and "sementara itu" reads as "meanwhile"; it should be "Untuk sementara, anggap". In 246, "Kesalahan energi dari keadaan ini karena itu adalah" copies the English word order, and in 151 "berbeda lebih sedikit" is a stiff calque of "differ less".

examples.source: Temporarily assume $r$ is even: then define $d=r/2$.
examples.translation: Sementara itu anggap $r$ genap: maka definisikan $d=r/2$.
examples.suggested: Untuk sementara, anggap $r$ genap; lalu definisikan $d=r/2$.
examples.why: 'Sementara itu' means 'meanwhile', not 'temporarily'. It hides the point that this is a provisional assumption that gets lifted later for odd r.

examples.source: The energy error of this state is therefore
examples.translation: Kesalahan energi dari keadaan ini karena itu adalah
examples.suggested: Dengan demikian, kesalahan energi keadaan ini adalah
examples.why: 'karena itu' sits in the middle of the sentence, copying English word order. It reads as machine translation.

examples.source: since the Krylov basis vectors differ less from timestep to timestep
examples.translation: karena vektor-vektor basis Krylov berbeda lebih sedikit dari satu langkah waktu ke langkah waktu berikutnya
examples.suggested: karena perbedaan vektor-vektor basis Krylov antarlangkah waktu makin kecil
examples.why: 'berbeda lebih sedikit' is a stiff calque of 'differ less'. The meaning is still correct.

editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entries 144 and 198 are faithful and read naturally. A native editor would still fix a few things. Entry 8 drops the hedge in "we might occasionally use" ("kami sesekali menggunakan"), switches between "kami" and "kita" within the same sentence ("kami ... mengacu ... dari dataset kita"), and renders "at a time" with the calque "dalam satu waktu". Entry 141 has the English-shaped "Perhatikan, bagaimanapun, bahwa", and entry 84 ends with a stray "pula" for "anyway", which reads oddly in Indonesian.

examples.line_approx: Dalam pelajaran ini, kami sesekali menggunakan ... dari dataset kita dalam satu waktu
examples.source: In this lesson, we might occasionally use these notations ... But we will mostly refer to the loading of a single vector from our dataset at a time
examples.translation: Dalam pelajaran ini, kami sesekali menggunakan notasi ... Tapi kami sebagian besar akan mengacu pada loading satu vektor dari dataset kita dalam satu waktu
examples.suggested: Dalam pelajaran ini, kita mungkin sesekali memakai notasi ... Namun, sebagian besar kita akan membahas loading satu vektor dari dataset kita pada satu waktu (satu per satu)
examples.why: The hedge 'might' is dropped. The kami/kita switch inside one sentence is jarring, and 'dalam satu waktu' is a calque.

examples.line_approx: Perhatikan, bagaimanapun, bahwa setiap prefaktor bersifat kompleks!
examples.source: Note, however, that each prefactor is complex!
examples.translation: Perhatikan, bagaimanapun, bahwa setiap prefaktor bersifat kompleks!
examples.suggested: Namun, perhatikan bahwa setiap prefaktor bernilai kompleks!
examples.why: 'Perhatikan, bagaimanapun, bahwa' copies the English word order. A native technical writer would put 'Namun' first.

examples.source: especially since data should be rescaled to the $(0,2\pi]$ interval, anyway.
examples.translation: terutama karena data harus diskalakan ulang ke interval $(0,2\pi]$ pula.
examples.suggested: terutama karena toh data memang sebaiknya diskalakan ulang ke interval $(0,2\pi]$.
examples.why: 'pula' means 'also' and does not carry the sense of 'anyway'. Ending the sentence with it reads awkwardly.

examples.line_approx: kondisi normalisasi yang dipaksakan oleh mekanika kuantum
examples.source: This is the normalization condition imposed by quantum mechanics:
examples.translation: Ini adalah kondisi normalisasi yang dipaksakan oleh mekanika kuantum:
examples.suggested: Ini adalah syarat normalisasi yang diharuskan oleh mekanika kuantum:
examples.why: 'dipaksakan' suggests something forced on you unwillingly. For a physical constraint, 'diharuskan' or 'disyaratkan' is the usual technical wording.

editor_note: Entry 11 (the Credly notice) is faithful, including the data list, "anak perusahaan dan pihak ketiga IBM secara global" and both privacy-statement links. Entry 4 does not mislead but has two small slips. First, "assume some familiarity" became "sudah cukup familiar", and "cukup" can read as "fairly/sufficiently familiar", which slightly raises the prerequisite. Second, the topic list translates only the first item: "pengkodean data" is in Indonesian, but "quantum kernels" and "variational quantum circuits" are left in English. The natural Indonesian terms are "kernel kuantum" and "sirkuit kuantum variasional".

examples.source: but will also assume some familiarity with these methods
examples.translation: tapi juga mengasumsikan kamu sudah cukup familiar dengan metode-metode tersebut
examples.suggested: tapi juga mengasumsikan kamu sudah sedikit mengenal metode-metode tersebut
examples.why: 'cukup familiar' can read as 'sufficiently familiar', which is a slightly stronger prerequisite than the English 'some familiarity'.

examples.source: Topics include data encoding, quantum kernels, and variational quantum circuits.
examples.translation: Topik mencakup pengkodean data, quantum kernels, dan variational quantum circuits.
examples.suggested: Topiknya mencakup pengkodean data, kernel kuantum, dan sirkuit kuantum variasional.
examples.why: Only the first topic is translated and the other two stay in English with the English plural, so the list is inconsistent. Indonesian QML texts use 'kernel kuantum' and 'sirkuit kuantum variasional'.

editor_note: All five rewritten entries (16, 19, 21, 40, 53) keep the English meaning, including the barren-plateau caveat in [21] and the SWAP-gate reasoning in [19], so nothing here would mislead a learner. The problems are terminology consistency and one small shift in tone. Entry [53] uses the fully Indonesianized "sirkuit kuantum" while the rest of the page uses "quantum circuit"/"Circuit kuantum". Entry [16] writes both "variational" and "variasional" in the same paragraph. In [53], "We could keep in mind" became "Kita perlu ingat" ("we need to remember"), which turns an optional side remark into an instruction.

examples.source: In mapping our problem to a quantum circuit
examples.translation: Saat memetakan masalah kita ke sebuah sirkuit kuantum
examples.suggested: Saat memetakan masalah kita ke quantum circuit
examples.why: Everywhere else the page uses 'quantum circuit'/'Circuit kuantum'. 'sirkuit kuantum' appears only here, so the page's terminology becomes inconsistent.

examples.source: This variational circuit is sometimes called the "ansatz" ... multiple variational and/or encoding layers
examples.translation: Circuit variational ini kadang disebut "ansatz" ... beberapa layer variasional dan/atau encoding
examples.suggested: Circuit variational ini ... beberapa layer variational dan/atau encoding
examples.why: The same paragraph spells the term two ways, 'variational' and 'variasional'. One spelling should be used throughout.

examples.source: We could keep in mind that adding CNOT gates ... may also be useful.
examples.translation: Kita perlu ingat bahwa menambahkan Gate CNOT ... mungkin juga berguna.
examples.suggested: Kita bisa tetap mengingat bahwa menambahkan Gate CNOT ... mungkin juga berguna.
examples.why: 'could' becomes 'perlu' (need to), so an optional side remark reads as an instruction. This is minor because the 'mungkin' hedge is kept.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The subtle parts survive intact, including the XX refocusing argument, the caveat that DD can lower fidelity at short idle times, and the explanation of why twirling makes the GHZ result worse. The problem is terminology that changes partway through. The first ~75% uses Indonesian renderings (sirkuit, fidelitas, lapisan, pelajaran, penekanan error, two-qubit gate), but from about entry [141] on it switches to English (circuit, fidelity, layer, lesson, *error suppression*, gate dua-qubit). "Dynamical decoupling" is also "Dekopling dinamis" in its heading but left in English in the body. There are a few small slips as well: entry [0] opens with exclusive "Kami" while the rest uses "kita", and entry [137] has the calque "error Pauli tipe stokastik".

examples.source: In this sense, the GHZ circuit enjoys an accidental coherence protection
examples.translation: Dalam hal ini, circuit GHZ memiliki proteksi koherensi yang tidak disengaja
examples.suggested: Dalam hal ini, sirkuit GHZ memiliki perlindungan koherensi yang tidak disengaja
examples.why: Earlier entries consistently use 'sirkuit' and 'perlindungan' (e.g. [138], [139]). From this point on the file switches to 'circuit', 'fidelity', 'layer' and 'lesson', although it used 'fidelitas', 'lapisan' and 'pelajaran' before.

examples.source: Throughout this lesson ... it might be described as *error suppression*
examples.translation: Sepanjang lesson ini, ... ia bisa disebut *error suppression*
examples.suggested: Sepanjang pelajaran ini, ... ia bisa disebut *penekanan error*
examples.why: The page title and body render the concept as 'penekanan error' and use 'pelajaran' for lesson. Reverting to English here breaks the terminology the page itself set up.

examples.source: Dynamical decoupling
examples.translation: Dekopling dinamis
examples.suggested: Dynamical decoupling
examples.why: The heading translates the term, but every body mention ([8], [32], [33], [48], [49]) keeps 'dynamical decoupling'. A learner may not connect the two.

examples.source: We explore techniques for suppressing some kinds of errors
examples.translation: Kami mengeksplorasi teknik untuk menekan beberapa jenis error
examples.suggested: Kita mengeksplorasi teknik untuk menekan beberapa jenis error
examples.why: Exclusive 'Kami' shuts out the reader. Everywhere else the page uses inclusive 'kita'.

examples.source: reshapes coherent, systematic errors into stochastic Pauli-type errors
examples.translation: membentuk ulang error koheren dan sistematis menjadi error Pauli tipe stokastik
examples.suggested: membentuk ulang error koheren dan sistematis menjadi error stokastik bertipe Pauli
examples.why: This is a calqued word order: 'Pauli tipe stokastik' misplaces the modifier. The meaning is 'stochastic errors of Pauli type'.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally. The hedge in the exam note survives ("badge dan ujian seharusnya siap saat kursus lengkap sudah tersedia"), and "tools mana yang bisa digunakan bersama, dan mana yang saling bertentangan" keeps the English contrast between tools that combine and tools that conflict.

The four rewritten entries (3, 4, 8, 9) keep the English meaning and none of them would mislead a learner. A native editor would still change three calques. In entry 4, "bersifat tangensial terhadap" copies the English "tangential to"; "tidak berkaitan langsung dengan" is more natural Indonesian. In entry 9, "aset instruksional" is a literal rendering of "instructional assets"; the usual term is "materi ajar". In entry 8, "dengan itikad baik" is tacked onto the end of the clause, which reads stiffly; "Estimasi ... yang dibuat sebaik mungkin" would read better. Entry 3 is faithful and natural.

examples.source: they are mostly tangential to the utility-scale calculation to which we are building
examples.translation: sebagian besar bersifat tangensial terhadap perhitungan skala utilitas yang sedang kita bangun
examples.suggested: sebagian besar tidak berkaitan langsung dengan perhitungan skala utilitas yang sedang kita tuju
examples.why: This is a calque of 'tangential to'. The phrase 'bersifat tangensial terhadap' is not how Indonesian technical prose says 'only loosely related'.

examples.source: these instructional assets
examples.translation: aset instruksional ini
examples.suggested: materi ajar ini
examples.why: 'Aset instruksional' is a word-for-word rendering. Indonesian teaching material conventionally uses 'materi ajar' or 'bahan ajar'.

examples.source: Good-faith estimates of required QPU time have been provided at the top of each lesson
examples.translation: Estimasi waktu QPU yang diperlukan telah diberikan di bagian atas setiap pelajaran dengan itikad baik
examples.suggested: Estimasi waktu QPU yang diperlukan, yang dibuat sebaik mungkin, telah dicantumkan di bagian atas setiap pelajaran
examples.why: Putting 'dengan itikad baik' at the end of the clause is stiff. It also attaches the good faith to the act of providing the estimates rather than to the estimates themselves.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning: entry 32 correctly says the new synthesis gives a shallower circuit, and entry 61 keeps level 2/3, the three pass names and the comparison with level 1. Two small phrasing slips remain. In entry 61, "untuk optimasi yang lebih banyak" is a word-for-word calque of "for more optimization", and "optimasi lebih lanjut" is the natural Indonesian. In entry 32, "lebih dangkal (shallower)" adds an English gloss that "lebih dangkal" does not need; it could also be tied to "kedalaman" (depth), which the page uses elsewhere.

examples.source: for more optimization, namely two-qubit block optimization
examples.translation: untuk optimasi yang lebih banyak, yaitu optimasi blok dua-Qubit
examples.suggested: untuk optimasi lebih lanjut, yaitu optimasi blok dua-qubit
examples.why: 'optimasi yang lebih banyak' is a stiff word-for-word calque of 'more optimization'. 'Optimasi lebih lanjut' is what an Indonesian technical writer would write.

examples.source: The new synthesis produces a shallower circuit. Why?
examples.translation: Sintesis baru menghasilkan circuit yang lebih dangkal (shallower). Kenapa?
examples.suggested: Sintesis baru menghasilkan circuit yang lebih dangkal (kedalamannya lebih kecil). Kenapa?
examples.why: The English gloss '(shallower)' is unnecessary. A gloss tied to 'kedalaman' (depth), the term the page uses elsewhere, would link the idea to circuit depth better.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries match their English and read naturally: [4] renders "some experience" as "sudah memiliki sedikit pengalaman" and keeps "IBM Quantum primitives", and [11] keeps the Credly notice complete ("prosesor data pihak ketiga", "anak perusahaan dan pihak ketiga IBM secara global"), with no caveat dropped.
